findings.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock (check-then-act gap after RUnlock), so concurrent cold-start callers each re-read the manifest serially instead of reusing the value the first one cached

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — Cache is set to result unconditionally, even on error, so a caller that lost the race and hit a transient load failure overwrites a good cached value with nil and returns nil plus an error

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Nothing re-checks the cache after Lock(), so N concurrent cold-start misses queue on the write lock and each one re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json in turn (thundering herd plus serialized latency).

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On error, result is nil and gets cached as nil, so after a manifest failure every page load takes the exclusive lock and hits disk again, all behind one global mutex.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — In Dev mode every call skips the cache and takes the exclusive write lock for disk read and JSON decode, which serializes all concurrent index page loads (the RLock read before it does nothing in this mode).

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent cold-cache requests queue up and each redo the manifest read serially instead of reusing the first result.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On read failure the cache is overwritten with nil and the error is not cached, so every subsequent request re-takes the exclusive lock and retries the file read, serializing all page renders behind repeated failing I/O with no backoff.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:56 — Exclusive lock is held across readWebAssetsFromCDN, which uses http.DefaultClient with no timeout, so a hung CDN fetch would block every GetWebAssets caller (currently latent since cdn is hardcoded "").
pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Lock() does not honor ctx cancellation, so requests whose context is cancelled still block waiting behind a slow in-progress reload.
pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — In Dev mode every call bypasses the cache and takes the exclusive write lock plus file I/O, fully serializing all concurrent index renders.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:41 — The concurrency fix ships without any test (pkg/api/webassets has no _test.go), so no parallel GetWebAssets test exercises the RWMutex under `go test -race` to prove the data race is gone.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Nothing re-checks the cache after taking the write lock and no test covers it, so concurrent cold-cache callers all re-read the manifest one after another. A concurrent-miss test with a call counter would catch this.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — The error path writes a nil result into the cache, which wipes a previously good cache (for example on a Dev-mode reload failure), and no test asserts what the cache holds after a failure.
pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — No test covers the branching: a non-Dev cache hit that skips the file read, versus Dev mode that always re-reads the manifest.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:37 — The cache is package-level global state with no reset hook, so any future tests would share it and depend on run order unless the code gets a reset helper or an injectable cache.

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Nothing re-checks the cache after Lock(), so N concurrent cold-start misses queue on the write lock and each one re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json in turn (thundering herd plus serialized latency).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RLock fast-path and then unconditionally takes a write Lock() on cache miss, but it does not re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring the write lock. As shown, multiple concurrent callers can all observe `ret == nil`, then serialize on the write lock and each proceed to do the expensive work under the lock (reading/parsing assets) rather than the first populating the cache and later callers returning immediately. This is a performance/latency concern (thundering herd + serialized work), not a functional correctness bug proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On error, result is nil and gets cached as nil, so after a manifest failure every page load takes the exclusive lock and hits disk again, all behind one global mutex.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and takes an exclusive `Lock()` after a cache miss (`ret == nil`) without re-checking the cache under the write lock, and the lock is held across the subsequent work (disk/manifest parsing happens while locked, since `defer Unlock()` is immediately after `Lock()`). If the cache remains nil (e.g., due to repeated manifest failures), every call will serialize behind this one mutex and redo the expensive work. The claim that it explicitly "caches nil" isn’t verifiable from the shown hunk, but the serialized-disk-on-miss behavior is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — In Dev mode every call skips the cache and takes the exclusive write lock for disk read and JSON decode, which serializes all concurrent index page loads (the RLock read before it does nothing in this mode).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RWMutex and, when `cfg.Env == setting.Dev`, the early return is skipped (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && ret != nil`). In that case the code always proceeds to `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` and holds the exclusive lock for the remainder of `GetWebAssets` (which will include the disk read/JSON decode later in the function). This will serialize concurrent callers in Dev mode, and the initial `RLock` read provides no benefit in that mode. This is a real performance/concurrency concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On read failure the cache is overwritten with nil and the error is not cached, so every subsequent request re-takes the exclusive lock and retries the file read, serializing all page renders behind repeated failing I/O with no backoff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds a global RWMutex and takes an exclusive `Lock()` on every cache miss (after the initial `RLock`/read), with no double-check inside the write lock. If the subsequent load/build of assets fails and the cache remains `nil` (the diff shows no mechanism to cache failures), every later request will again take the exclusive lock and retry the expensive work, serializing callers during persistent failure. However, the specific claim that the cache is explicitly "overwritten with nil" on read failure is not shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:56 — Exclusive lock is held across readWebAssetsFromCDN, which uses http.DefaultClient with no timeout, so a hung CDN fetch would block every GetWebAssets caller (currently latent since cdn is hardcoded "").

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds an exclusive `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` with `defer Unlock()` before the function proceeds to compute `result`, meaning the write lock will be held across the remaining work in `GetWebAssets` (potentially including slow I/O like reading assets or network fetches). That can unnecessarily serialize/block all callers while one goroutine does the work. However, the finding’s specific claim about `readWebAssetsFromCDN` using `http.DefaultClient` with no timeout and CDN being hardcoded cannot be verified from the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Lock() does not honor ctx cancellation, so requests whose context is cancelled still block waiting behind a slow in-progress reload.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and unconditionally takes entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() on the reload path (after the initial RLock/RUnlock). sync.RWMutex has no context-aware acquisition, so a caller whose ctx is cancelled will still block waiting for the write lock if another goroutine is doing a slow reload while holding it. This is a diff-grounded behavioral concern (potentially increased request latency / blocked goroutines), but it’s not a clearly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone since no requirement is shown that ctx cancellation must abort waiting for cache reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — In Dev mode every call bypasses the cache and takes the exclusive write lock plus file I/O, fully serializing all concurrent index renders.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RWMutex and unconditionally takes an exclusive Lock() (with defer Unlock()) before recomputing assets when the early-return cache path is not taken. Since the early return is gated by `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`, in Dev mode it will always bypass the cache and then hold the write lock during the subsequent work (which likely includes file I/O later in the function), thus serializing concurrent calls. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/concurrency concern, not a correctness bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:41 — The concurrency fix ships without any test (pkg/api/webassets has no _test.go), so no parallel GetWebAssets test exercises the RWMutex under `go test -race` to prove the data race is gone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new concurrency behavior (a global RWMutex guarding the global `entryPointAssetsCache` and new lock/unlock logic in `GetWebAssets`). The PR diff does not include any accompanying tests that exercise concurrent calls (e.g., under `-race`) to validate the fix. The claim that the package has no existing `_test.go` files is not verifiable from this diff alone, but the absence of new tests in this change is directly observable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Nothing re-checks the cache after taking the write lock and no test covers it, so concurrent cold-cache callers all re-read the manifest one after another. A concurrent-miss test with a call counter would catch this.

adjudication.rationale: In GetWebAssets, the function reads entryPointAssetsCache under an RLock, but if it’s nil it unconditionally takes the write Lock and proceeds without re-checking the cache under the write lock. From the diff shown, this means concurrent callers during a cold cache can all pass the initial RLock check (ret == nil) and then, one-by-one under the write lock, repeat the expensive manifest computation instead of letting the first populate the cache and the rest return it. This is a real, diff-grounded concurrency/performance issue, not a correctness failure. The claim about lacking a test isn’t verifiable from this diff alone, but the missing double-check is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — The error path writes a nil result into the cache, which wipes a previously good cache (for example on a Dev-mode reload failure), and no test asserts what the cache holds after a failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows adding an RWMutex and wrapping the cache read/check plus taking a write lock; it does not show any code that writes `result` (nil or otherwise) into `entryPointAssetsCache`, nor any error-handling path. Therefore the claim that an error path writes a nil result into the cache and wipes a previously good cache is not verifiable from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — No test covers the branching: a non-Dev cache hit that skips the file read, versus Dev mode that always re-reads the manifest.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows added caching/locking logic in GetWebAssets (RLock/RUnlock, cache hit return, then Lock). It does not show any test files or coverage info, so the claim that "no test covers" the Dev vs non-Dev cache-hit branching cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:37 — The cache is package-level global state with no reset hook, so any future tests would share it and depend on run order unless the code gets a reset helper or an injectable cache.

adjudication.rationale: The diff keeps `entryPointAssetsCache` as a package-level global (`var (...) entryPointAssetsCache *dtos.EntryPointAssets`) and even notes `// TODO: get rid of global state`. There is no reset/injection hook shown, so any tests calling `GetWebAssets` could observe shared cached state across runs. This is an architectural/testability concern, not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff.
